title: Dispensing regularity and the controlled-agreement fill interval on Prescriptions & Renewals
content:
**To dispensing pharmacies — Prescriptions & Renewals controlled prescriptions.**

When the patient signs a new controlled-substance agreement, the dispensing-regularity allowance follows the number of dispensings of the prescription in the last 12 calendar months: 11 or 12 dispensings allow 28 days; 9 or 10 dispensings allow 21 days; any other number allows the starting 14 days.

**What is counted.** Each dispensing of this prescription whose dispensing date falls within the 12 calendar months before the signing day counts once, whatever its days' supply or dispensing basis. Authorizations and voids are not dispensings.

| Dispensings in the 12 months | Dispensing-regularity allowance |
|---|---|
| 0 to 8 | 14 days |
| 9 or 10 | 21 days |
| 11 or 12 | 28 days |
| 13 or more | 14 days |

**Notes.**
1. The two upper bands are closed at both ends: 9 and 10 give 21 days, 11 and 12 give 28 days.
2. A count above 12 falls under "any other number" and gives 14 days, as does a count of 8 or fewer.
